rounds.text: RBZ Jewellers is currently trading at a significant valuation discount, with a P/E ratio of 9.53x compared to a sector benchmark of 28.56x [E1, E6]. This undervaluation is underscored by a price-to-book ratio of 1.80x, which sits below the sector benchmark of 2.09x despite the company delivering exceptional growth metrics [E2, E7]. The firm has demonstrated consistent operational excellence, evidenced by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 42% and a 54% increase in profit over the trailing twelve months [E17, E19]. Management is actively positioning the company for future expansion, as shown by a 733.3% surge in capital work in progress and explicit revenue guidance targeting INR 800 to 900 crores for FY27 [E34, E71]. While the company is currently in a high-growth phase, it is important to note that the stock has experienced a 3% decline in price over the last year [E20]. Conceded: the company currently offers a dividend yield of 0.00% and reported a 12% year-on-year decline in wholesale revenue for the most recent quarter [E4, E86].

Despite headline growth metrics, the bear case rests on cracks in core operational segments and warning flags regarding momentum [E61, E86]. Management noted that wholesale revenue declined by 12% year-on-year to INR70 crores for the quarter, alongside a steeper 46% year-on-year drop in job work revenue to approximately INR2 crores [E86]. Furthermore, the signal engine explicitly flags that earnings growth is decelerating [E61], while the share price reflects this disconnect with a compounded 1-year return of -3% [E20]. Compounding these headwinds, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00%, returning nothing to shareholders despite its expanding capital base [E4]. Capital-intensive expansion is also underway with Capital Work in Progress surging by 733.3% to Rs 25 Cr for March 2026, which introduces execution and capital allocation risks as these projects scale up [E34]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing sales growth of 30% and robust 5-year profit growth alongside a low P/E multiple [E1, E16, E54].

Conceded: wholesale revenue declined by 12% to INR70 crores and job work revenue fell 46% to INR2 crores [E86]. However, this segment friction is vastly outweighed by massive top-line expansion, with 5-year sales compounded at 43% [E14], 3-year sales at 30% [E15], and trailing twelve month sales matching that 30% pace [E16], drastically outperforming the sector median sales growth of 17.7% [E68]. While the bear highlights decelerating earnings signals and a -3% one-year share price return [E20, E61], trailing twelve month profit growth actually accelerated to 54% [E19], completely eclipsing the 1-year share price return and triggering a price-led signal where profit growth exceeds price growth by 57% [E51]. The 733.3% surge in CWIP to Rs 25 Cr [E34] is not an unmanaged risk, but rather the deliberate growth spend required to fuel management's guidance of INR800 crores to INR900 crores in revenue for FY27 [E71], backed by retail expansion in Surat projected to deliver INR150 crores [E72] and new 5,000 square foot stores in Eastern Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar [E78]. Finally, the absence of dividends [E4] is entirely justified for a high-return business generating an 11.68% ROA—nearly four times the sector benchmark of 3.1% [E8]—while trading at an ultra-low P/E of 9.53x [E1] compared to the sector benchmark of 28.56x [E6].

Conceded: the 5-year sales growth is 43% [E14], 3-year sales growth is 30% [E15], and trailing twelve month profit growth stands at 54% [E19]. However, the scanX signal engine explicitly flags that earnings growth is decelerating [E61], directly contradicting the notion of unblemished operational acceleration. Furthermore, the 733.3% surge in CWIP to Rs 25 Cr introduces substantial execution risk for uncompleted projects [E34], and the market has correctly noted these headwinds as the share price has delivered a negative 3% return over the past year [E20]. This negative price action persists despite the price-led signal [E51], showing that investors remain deeply sceptical of management's future projections. Finally, the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], meaning shareholders bear all the risks of aggressive capex expansion and wholesale revenue contractions [E86] without any immediate cash return.
